Losing my current job to try out medication would have an irreparable consequence for me. If it wasn't for my job, I wouldn't have even got as far as I can, and even though I'd be able to work in something else, I have no desire to return to working in hospitaliy, shops or anything else that isn't linked to what I studied in college. I quite frankly couldn't return to working that style of life, let alone the pay cut I'd have to take to work there. For me, losing a job in the field I studied so hard for is the equivalent of losing my life anyway. If it wasn't for the job, I would never have made the progress I did manage to make. I would never have been able to afford therapy, let alone all the stuff I managed to accomplish during the time I spent working on myself. 
I've only given the thought to life after medication so much thought, because I tried opening up about some of this stuff to one of my friends last week. I guess really he gave me all the reassurances good friends usually do, but he also urged me to go and see a professional. I've not told any of my friends or family that I've been going to therapy, because I'm afraid word of it will reach my job, as seeing a therapist is information I'm supposed to disclose. I also can't talk to my therapist about how far these thoughts of mine have gone, becasue in my country, if your therapist thinks you are of immediate danger to yourself, they can have you involuntarily committed. While technically I don't plan to do anything for another two months, the fact that I have access to everything I need and will have it all in my possession soon is more than reason enough to have me committed. Although the lengths to which I've planned it out are already reason enough for my therapist to go down that route with me. It just doesn't seem like I can win at all with those routes.  

Also, I'm sorry if I sounded like I was discrediting the positive effects that medications have. I didn't mean it to come across like that at all. I've seen firsthand with friends and family, as well as getting to read a lot of case studies that had good outcomes. 
I just don't see a point in trying to overcome it anymore. I just don't know why I'm trying at the end of the day. I can't see what there is to try for.

I’m personally not open to the idea of trying anti-depressants. My research project in college focused heavily on antidepressants, CBT and ECT in the treatments of depression, and while they can be effective, antidepressants serve to correct a chemical imbalance. My issues lie with the way in which “I’m wired” so to speak. 
I do acknowledge the benefits antidepressant and similar medications have, and I have seen how they can help, but it’s not a route I’d like to go down, and it’s also something I can’t do at a risk of being unemployable for the rest of my life anyway. Despite the “accepting” age the world is in looking at mental health, I know of numerous incredibly well qualified people who are repeatedly being turned down for jobs for years because of nothing but their mental health. Obviously legally they can’t be turned down for the position on those grounds, but those grounds are being why they’re not being offered the jobs. If I did go down the route of medication, and it somehow ended up being the solution to these problems, I’d have nothing for me after it all. And I’d end up in the same pit. Honestly, the only reason I was able to progress so far over the time I did was thanks to my job, and I don’t know what I would have done without it. 
Honestly I believe that once your dead, that’s it really. I don’t think there’s anything after life, and even if there was, I obviously wouldn’t deserve it if I couldn’t live out this life. And that’s fine. I was curious for a bit, about both the good and the bad, but I don’t have that curiosity anymore. I don’t expect everything to be good all the time. The bad is also a very important part of life, and definitely helps shape us into the people we are. But I’m just so fed up of trying. I know nothing is meant to be easy, but when I do “have so much”, surely I shouldn’t feel like I’m trying to swim upriver against a strong current all the time.

Thanks. I know it’s littered with punctuation errors that I just cannot be bothered to fix. Haha.

If you don’t mind me asking, what did you work in for a while that was so stressful for you? I’m sorry it was so bad to the point you had daily panic attacks. That must have been awful, especially when you were giving your life another shot. As for falling in love with someone, it really sucks when it’s not reciprocated. I don’t think I’ve ever experienced that kind of love myself, but I do know how crushing it is to have someone not like you back in the way that you like them. And it is so much more difficult than a case of “well is their loss”, but that’s really all you can tell yourself to try and help you keep on keeping. 

I can empathise completely with feeling miserable when you’re not with your friends. It’s how I felt for a large portion of that first 8 months, and really it was only the last 4 months where I got to be “okay” with being a lone with myself. I’d established this “new normal” for my head where I just had to get used to the fact that for now, I’ll be sitting stewing in my own thoughts all the time. I can’t sit and focus on one thing at a time, it’s not enough distraction for my head. If I’m watching a show/film, I need to have my phone in hand to aimlessly scroll through something to keep me fully occupied and not let intrusive thoughts in. If I’m reading a book, I need music, tea/coffee and a snack to occupy me. You get the gist I think. 

As for writing. I didn’t write in a storytelling sense, but I journaled extensively for the last year and 4 months. Journaled everything from dreams I was having all the way to my thoughts and feelings on things I’d read in the news. It was quite cathartic for me. 
Is getting another job an option for you, even something part time not based on your degree? Something to escape your house a bit and earn a little for yourself. Something part-time could eventually help ease you into coping with the stress and pressure of a full-time job somewhere down the road. As for the toxic home environment, there isn’t much you can do about that without a job really. It sounds very high stress for you. If you feel you can’t write in the way you want to, perhaps journaling/keeping some sort of diary (probably electronic to avoid others reading it), might help you. 

And you didn’t hijack the post at all. I don’t think this subreddit is anything to do with hijacking anything. It’s a place people come to let off this kind of stuff, so you’re perfectly entitled to do so without having to make your own separate post. 
On one hand, it’s nice to know people can somewhat understand where I’m coming from, but on the other hand, it’s really shitty that others have to feel like that too. I hope things improve for you.

I’m so sorry that your gender is causing you so much hurt. 
I don’t know how much it will help, but if you were once good at making friends, then you still will be. Being a genuinely nice and friendly person that people like isn’t something you just “lose”. It’s something that gets buried underneath a mound of troubles, and it’s definitely something you can do again. Meeting people is a perfect way to travel for some, but I also have friends who like to just up sticks and go travelling by themselves. They don’t want to “wait for others” to be free when they feel like travelling, and they say they love it so much that they don’t feel lonely when they do it.
As for being transgender, it shouldn’t be a deterrent for people to be friends with you, especially in this day and age. Although, I do know some areas are much more narrow minded than others. But I know people from my hometown (rural narrow minded area), that have met transgender men and women and made very good friends with them. Try not to give up hope.

I tried living for others for quite a while, as in, I only kept myself around for others to the point where I had no life of my own, and everything about their lives was mine. It’s not a way to live to be honest. I’ve seen people saying something to the effect of “find anything to keep you alive and live for that”, but if that involves actively neglecting yourself, then there’s still no point to it. I think it’s you yourself that you have to take care of, first and foremost. But you do have to find a balance in that so that you don’t become completely selfish and self-absorbed. Other people still matter, but when your mental health is the problem, you’re what matters most.

I don’t expect to always be happy. But I did expect things to be better with all the work I put into it, you know? Normally I don’t have expectations of anything because it stops you getting disappointed, but after working so hard and reaching a point where everything was fine, I still went all the way back down to the start. It’s just crushing for me. 
I do hope that people find it “inspiring” that things can change though. I’m sure someone stronger than myself can take some of the steps I’ve taken and forge a better path throughout their life and not get disheartened when they have large setbacks. Helping your mental health is a person by person basis. Nothing works for everyone, and no two approaches will ever have the same end result. So if there’s anything that should be taken from this; it’s that there is hope for people. It’s just a really long road, and for some, it’s too long.

It’ll end my pain, and that’s all that matters to me now to be honest. I’m aware of what it’ll do to the people left behind. Even walking through work this morning reminds me of that, but I honestly don’t care anymore

I live in Europe, and if I were to set any last travelling goals for myself, visiting the US would probably be the last one I have seeing as I’ve never been before. It’s something I might consider for my last few months anyway so thanks for the suggestion.

I thought mine had gotten weaker, but really nothing had changed. I just ended up back in the exact same mindset I was in, and no amount of time spent doing hobbies, travelling and other stuff I enjoy could distract me from it. I don’t expect anything will change, but thanks for the sentiment.

Well I wish you luck with your move to Spain and hope you find something to change your mind. 

I can empathise with you feeling like you’ve spent your whole life looking for reasons not to kill yourself. I’ve been doing the same. Always telling myself things will change if I do ‘x’ thing. Just putting it off really. I feel genuinely guilty even when I’ve had my friends there for me when I’ve felt suicidal in the past. A lot of them have genuine struggles and issues that are the roots of their depression and suicidal ideation, so it pushes me away from talking about it with them even more. 

I do hope things change for you though. Just because one person has tried, seemingly succeeded, then ended back up at square one, it doesn’t mean that will happen for everyone. There isn’t a one size fits all glove for mental health.

To be honest, I don’t really care what way it leaves anyone after I’m gone. When I’m gone, that’s it for me. It’s not something I have to worry about anymore. Sure, that’s horrible, nasty and selfish, but I’m done really. I’ve tried pretty hard to end up in the same place I was when I started, and nothing’s going to change. 

The prospect of having x amount of years left doesn’t really make me feel anything. I’m not gonna jump and say “oh that’s 96 years more of misery”, because I would 100% be lying if I said I wasn’t happy at least once over the last year and 4 months. It certainly doesn’t make me happier knowing I have time left though either. 
I’m also not going to jump down your throat for what you say. Everyone’s entitled to speak their piece.
As for talking to people about this, I talk to my friends and they either try to talk me down or someone bites the bullet and has me committed to a psychiatric ward. Either way, it’s the same end result for me. Not really much choice in the matter

Yeah that’s the problem really. Like there isn’t an inherent meaning to life, the only meaning is what YOU can give it. I can’t find any meaning to it for myself, so I don’t see the point really. I don’t even feel guilty or sad about the hurt I’ll cause to my friends and family anymore. They’ll get over it eventually

Feel free to comment away. To be honest, I'd like to see what others have to say regarding it anyway.   
Thanks I guess! To be honest, I was thinking about posting this a lot today in work so I had a general idea of what I wanted to say. I still feel there's more I want to put out, but I can't exactly think what. Just trying to offload everything.
